# Connector templates

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_connector_template_docs.py from apps/python-executor/app/connector_templates.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Prebuilt decision-time connectors for named providers. Install one with
`POST /api/v1/connector-templates/{id}/install`; list them with
`GET /api/v1/connector-templates`. Each installs a connector with `fetch_at_decision` on and
`on_fetch_failure: review_gate`, plus starter variables in `dev`.

**None of these has been run against the provider's live sandbox** — that needs credentials
the provider issues to a customer. Each was built from the provider's published contract, and
is tested end to end against a local server serving the provider's own documented example
bodies. Every template lists what was and was not verified.

A source a policy never reaches is not fetched, even with every variable computed: installing
a bureau template does not turn unrelated decisions into bureau pulls.

## Equifax — US Consumer Credit Report (JSON API)

`equifax_us_consumer_credit_report` · category `bureau` · region US · default connector id `equifax_ccr`

Pull an Equifax consumer credit report: hit status, the score for the model you are contracted for, trades and inquiries. OAuth2 client credentials.

Sources: [guide](https://assets.equifax.com/acro-migration-kb/assets/consumer_credit_json_api_getting_started_guide.pdf) · [spec](https://github.com/fullstack-development/haskell-equifax-generated/blob/master/openapi.yaml) · [portal](https://developer.equifax.com/products/apiproducts/oneview-consumer-credit-report)

### Verified (2026-09-24)

- OAuth2 client credentials, client id and secret sent as HTTP Basic, token used as Bearer -- Equifax's own quick start guide.
- Sandbox base URL, POST /reports/credit-report, and the scope https://api.equifax.com/business/consumer-credit/v1 -- Equifax's portal OpenAPI spec, as republished in a public repository (the portal itself requires a corporate-email login).
- Request envelope (consumers.name / socialNum / dateOfBirth / addresses, customerConfiguration.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport.memberNumber / securityCode / models / endUserInformation) -- that spec's published example.
- Response: status, consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[].hitCode, models[], trades[], inquiries[]; the full hitCode taxonomy; efxErrorCode error bodies for 400/401/403/404/415/500/501/503/504.

### Not verified

- Not run against Equifax's sandbox: client credentials are issued to a registered company.
- The token endpoint URL and the production/UAT base URLs are NOT in the public material, so the template takes them as install settings rather than guessing.
- The spec is Equifax's, but obtained from a third-party repository that generated a client from it; confirm against the portal's API Reference when you register.

### Contract discrepancies the template handles

- In Equifax's own example the FIRST model is an unrequested FICO Bankcard score and the REQUESTED model (02583) comes second, with score 0. A path like models[0].score reads the wrong model, so the template maps the whole models array and the starter variable selects by model number.
- status is documented as possibly "completed === Request Schema Validation Error": a 200 carrying a validation failure. The check requires exactly "completed".
- score is a string ("409") in one model and an integer (0) in another.

### Environments

| environment | base URL |
|---|---|
| sandbox | `https://api.sandbox.equifax.com/business/consumer-credit/v1` |

Any other environment needs `base_url` at install.

### Install settings and secrets

| key | kind | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token_url` | setting | yes | From your app's credentials page in the Equifax developer portal. |
| `client_id` | setting | yes | Equifax issues one per app and environment. |
| `member_number` | setting | yes | Your Equifax member number (test member numbers start with 999). |
| `model_id` | setting | yes | The model your contract returns, e.g. 02583 in Equifax's example. |
| `end_user_name` | setting | yes | endUserInformation.endUsersName -- the business the report is for. |
| `permissible_purpose_code` | setting | yes | FCRA permissible purpose, as agreed with Equifax. Default `01`. |
| `client_secret` | secret | yes | Sent to the token endpoint only, never to the report endpoint. |
| `security_code_secret` | secret | yes | The member number's security code, sent in the request body. |

### Decision inputs

| path | notes |
|---|---|
| `payload.custom.first_name` | First name. |
| `payload.custom.last_name` | Last name. |
| `payload.custom.ssn` | SSN. Must match `^[0-9]{9}$`. |
| `payload.custom.date_of_birth` | Date of birth (MMDDYYYY). Must match `^[0-9]{8}$`. |
| `payload.custom.house_number` | House number. |
| `payload.custom.street_name` | Street name. |
| `payload.custom.street_type` | Street type (LN, ST, AVE...). |
| `payload.custom.city` | City. |
| `payload.custom.state` | State. Must match `^[A-Za-z]{2}$`. |
| `payload.custom.zip` | ZIP. Must match `^[0-9]{5}$`. |

A missing input fails as `missing_input` and a malformed one as `invalid_input`, before any token request or provider call. The reason names the field, never the value.

### Request

`POST <base_url>/reports/credit-report`

```json
{
  "consumers": {
    "name": [
      {
        "identifier": "current",
        "firstName": "{{payload.custom.first_name}}",
        "lastName": "{{payload.custom.last_name}}"
      }
    ],
    "socialNum": [
      {
        "identifier": "current",
        "number": "{{payload.custom.ssn}}"
      }
    ],
    "dateOfBirth": "{{payload.custom.date_of_birth}}",
    "addresses": [
      {
        "identifier": "current",
        "houseNumber": "{{payload.custom.house_number}}",
        "streetName": "{{payload.custom.street_name}}",
        "streetType": "{{payload.custom.street_type}}",
        "city": "{{payload.custom.city}}",
        "state": "{{payload.custom.state}}",
        "zip": "{{payload.custom.zip}}"
      }
    ]
  },
  "customerReferenceIdentifier": "{{execution_id}}",
  "customerConfiguration": {
    "equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport": {
      "memberNumber": "<<member_number>>",
      "securityCode": "{{secrets.<<connector_id>>_security_code_secret}}",
      "codeDescriptionRequired": true,
      "models": [
        {
          "identifier": "<<model_id>>"
        }
      ],
      "endUserInformation": {
        "endUsersName": "<<end_user_name>>",
        "permissiblePurposeCode": "<<permissible_purpose_code>>"
      },
      "ECOAInquiryType": "Individual"
    }
  }
}
```

### Response → source fields

| field | path |
|---|---|
| `hit_code` | `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` |
| `file_since_date` | `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].fileSinceDate` |
| `models` | `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].models` |
| `trades` | `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].trades` |
| `inquiries` | `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].inquiries` |

### Error taxonomy

| when | code |
|---|---|
| 200, `$.status` is anything else outside `completed` | `equifax_transaction_not_completed` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `2` | `equifax_no_hit` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `9` | `equifax_no_hit` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `C` | `equifax_no_hit` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `3` | `equifax_manual_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `4` | `equifax_manual_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `D` | `equifax_manual_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `E` | `equifax_manual_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `5` | `equifax_referred_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `F` | `equifax_referred_file` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `A` | `equifax_file_frozen` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `G` | `equifax_file_frozen` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `L` | `equifax_file_locked` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `M` | `equifax_file_locked` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `I` | `equifax_inquiry_flagged_fraud` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is `J` | `equifax_inquiry_flagged_fraud` |
| 200, `$.consumers.equifaxUSConsumerCreditReport[0].hitCode.code` is anything else outside `1`, `6` | `equifax_unexpected_hit_code` |
| HTTP 400 | `equifax_bad_request` |
| HTTP 401 | `equifax_unauthorized` |
| HTTP 403 | `equifax_access_denied` |
| HTTP 404 | `equifax_not_found` |
| HTTP 415 | `equifax_unsupported_media_type` |
| HTTP 500 | `equifax_internal_error` |
| HTTP 501 | `equifax_not_implemented` |
| HTTP 503 | `equifax_unavailable` |
| HTTP 504 | `equifax_gateway_timeout` |
| any other non-2xx, transport failure, timeout | the engine's generic codes |

The provider's own error text (`$.efxErrorCode`, `$.description`) is carried in the failure reason, redacted.

Only 408, 429 and 5xx are retried; a 4xx is the provider's answer about this request and does not count against the circuit breaker.

### Starter variables (installed in `dev`)

| id | meaning |
|---|---|
| `<connector_id>_score` | The score of the contracted model, selected by model number -- never by position, because Equifax's own example puts an unrequested model first. Raises when that model is absent or reports no positive score, so the decision goes to review instead of deciding on 0. |
| `<connector_id>_past_due_total` | Sum of pastDueAmount over every reported trade. |
| `<connector_id>_trade_count` | Number of trades on the file. |

## FinBox — BankConnect predictors

`finbox_bankconnect_predictors` · category `bank_statement` · region IN · default connector id `finbox_bank`

Bank-statement predictors for an entity whose statements were uploaded to FinBox BankConnect: balances, salary, EMI outflow and cheque bounces.

Sources: [docs](https://docs.finbox.in/bank-connect/rest-api.html)

### Verified (2026-09-24)

- Base URL https://apis.bankconnect.finbox.in/bank-connect/v1/entity/<entity_id>/ and the x-api-key + server-hash headers.
- GET /predictors/ response: entity_id, progress (an ARRAY of {status, message, statement_id, source}), predictors (an array of {account_id, predictors}).
- Predictor keys avg_monthly_closing_balance, total_salary_0, total_emi_ecs_loan, inward_chq_bounces, outward_chq_bounces.
- progress.status is one of processing / completed / failed.
- 401 body {"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}.

### Not verified

- Not run against FinBox: API keys are issued by FinBox.
- The docs publish no sandbox host, so the template's only environment is production.
- Only 200 and 401 are documented. Other statuses fall back to the engine's generic codes rather than to names this template would have had to invent.
- Statements must already be uploaded (FinBox's upload or Account Aggregator flow); this template only reads the result, keyed by the entity id the caller supplies.

### Environments

| environment | base URL |
|---|---|
| production | `https://apis.bankconnect.finbox.in` |

Any other environment needs `base_url` at install.

### Install settings and secrets

| key | kind | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api_key` | secret | yes | Issued by FinBox. |
| `server_hash_secret` | secret | yes | Issued by FinBox. |

### Decision inputs

| path | notes |
|---|---|
| `payload.custom.finbox_entity_id` | The entity the customer's statements were uploaded under. Pattern-checked because it is placed in the URL path. Must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. |

A missing input fails as `missing_input` and a malformed one as `invalid_input`, before any token request or provider call. The reason names the field, never the value.

### Request

`GET <base_url>/bank-connect/v1/entity/{{payload.custom.finbox_entity_id}}/predictors/`

### Response → source fields

| field | path |
|---|---|
| `progress` | `$.progress` |
| `accounts` | `$.predictors` |

### Error taxonomy

| when | code |
|---|---|
| 200, `$.progress`[].status is `processing` | `finbox_statement_processing` |
| 200, `$.progress`[].status is `failed` | `finbox_statement_failed` |
| 200, `$.progress`[].status is anything else outside `completed` | `finbox_statement_not_completed` |
| 200, `$.predictors` has fewer than 1 item(s) | `finbox_no_accounts` |
| HTTP 401 | `finbox_unauthorized` |
| any other non-2xx, transport failure, timeout | the engine's generic codes |

The provider's own error text (`$.detail`) is carried in the failure reason, redacted.

Only 408, 429 and 5xx are retried; a 4xx is the provider's answer about this request and does not count against the circuit breaker.

### Starter variables (installed in `dev`)

| id | meaning |
|---|---|
| `<connector_id>_avg_monthly_closing_balance` | Summed across every account in the entity. |
| `<connector_id>_salary_last_month` | FinBox total_salary_0 (month_0 is the latest), summed across accounts. |
| `<connector_id>_emi_outflow` | FinBox total_emi_ecs_loan, summed across accounts. |
| `<connector_id>_inward_cheque_bounces` | FinBox inward_chq_bounces, summed across accounts. |

## Setu — PAN verification

`setu_pan_verification` · category `kyc` · region IN · default connector id `setu_pan`

Verify a customer's PAN against NSDL through Setu, with the name on record and Aadhaar seeding status.

Sources: [docs](https://docs.setu.co/data/pan/quickstart) · [spec](https://github.com/SetuHQ/docs/blob/main/api-references/data/pan.json)

### Verified (2026-09-24)

- Base URLs, endpoint, method and the three auth headers -- Setu's own OpenAPI 3.0 spec.
- Request fields pan / consent / reason, and that consent must be Y or y.
- Every response body the docs publish: valid PAN (200), invalid PAN (200), consent missing and reason too short (400), PAN not found (404), internal error (500).
- Sandbox test values: ABCDE1234A is valid, ABCDE1234B is invalid, anything else 404s.

### Not verified

- Not run against Setu's sandbox: x-client-id, x-client-secret and x-product-instance-id are issued by Setu on request.
- No 401 body is documented, so an auth failure surfaces as a generic auth_failed.

### Contract discrepancies the template handles

- The quickstart shows verification "success" / "failed" in lower case; the OpenAPI example shows "SUCCESS". The check accepts both cases rather than betting on one.

### Environments

| environment | base URL |
|---|---|
| sandbox | `https://dg-sandbox.setu.co` |
| production | `https://dg.setu.co` |

Any other environment needs `base_url` at install.

### Install settings and secrets

| key | kind | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | setting | yes | Issued by Setu with your credentials. |
| `product_instance_id` | setting | yes | Issued by Setu per product instance. |
| `reason` | setting | yes | Setu rejects a reason shorter than 20 characters (insufficient_reason_length). Default `Identity verification for a credit application`. |
| `client_secret` | secret | yes | Issued by Setu. |

### Decision inputs

| path | notes |
|---|---|
| `payload.custom.pan` | The customer's 10-character PAN. Must match `^[A-Za-z0-9]{10}$`. |
| `payload.custom.pan_consent` | Y when the customer consented to PAN verification. Supplied per application by the caller -- never hardcoded, because asserting consent that was not collected is the lender's liability, not a default. Must match `^[YyNn]$`. |

A missing input fails as `missing_input` and a malformed one as `invalid_input`, before any token request or provider call. The reason names the field, never the value.

### Request

`POST <base_url>/api/verify/pan`

```json
{
  "pan": "{{payload.custom.pan}}",
  "consent": "{{payload.custom.pan_consent}}",
  "reason": "<<reason>>"
}
```

### Response → source fields

| field | path |
|---|---|
| `verification` | `$.verification` |
| `message` | `$.message` |
| `full_name` | `$.data.full_name` |
| `category` | `$.data.category` |
| `aadhaar_seeding_status` | `$.data.aadhaar_seeding_status` |
| `trace_id` | `$.traceId` |

### Error taxonomy

| when | code |
|---|---|
| 200, `$.verification` is anything else outside `success`, `SUCCESS`, `failed`, `FAILED` | `setu_unexpected_verification_value` |
| HTTP 400 | `setu_bad_request` |
| HTTP 404 | `setu_pan_not_found` |
| HTTP 500 | `setu_internal_error` |
| any other non-2xx, transport failure, timeout | the engine's generic codes |

The provider's own error text (`$.error.code`, `$.message`) is carried in the failure reason, redacted.

Only 408, 429 and 5xx are retried; a 4xx is the provider's answer about this request and does not count against the circuit breaker.

### Starter variables (installed in `dev`)

| id | meaning |
|---|---|
| `<connector_id>_pan_verified` | True when Setu reports the PAN valid. An invalid PAN is False, not missing. |
| `<connector_id>_aadhaar_linked` | True/False from aadhaar_seeding_status. Setu marks the field optional; when it is absent this raises, so the decision goes to review instead of treating 'not reported' as 'not linked'. |
